column1: # The runner's own metric families: facts no runner verb carries, exported by
# `agentsfleet-runner run` straight to the runner collector. Same columns as
# docs/metrics.census.tsv and read by the same `Registry::read`; the daemon's
# census is untouched and neither file declares the other's families.
# `afr_telemetry` compiles this file in and grades it against its producers in
# ceiling against the product of its closed label sets
# fleet, lease, event or runner identifier: a label is a series that outlives
# the lease, and those identities belong on spans.
# Label sets: provider = the provider registry's names
# published tool catalog plus `_other` (40); signal and reason on the loss
# family are the daemon's own closed sets (3 x 6); every outcome and reason is

column11: model turn wall time by provider; one provider slow this hour stands out
turn sends retried; growth means a provider is rate limiting or failing
time to a sandbox whose executor answers; cold starts sit in the tail
live-tail frames lost on the runner; the run and its report are unaffected
memory pushes the daemon did not take, a mid-run checkpoint's included; the final push carries every entry again, so only one that fails there leaves the next run without them
tool call wall time by tool
tenant processes the kernel killed for memory inside a sandbox; the sandbox and the lease live on, so a rising count means fleets need more memory, not that hosts are failing
sandboxes held frozen between a fleet's leases, by what became of each: a falling reused share against parked means follow-ups arrive after the window or land elsewhere
spans the runner's span budget shed; a storm stays visible
telemetry the runner lost before its collector took it, counted at the source; a down collector shows here and nowhere else
